pull_request.title: Reuse validated nodes during page reclamation
pull_request.body:
Merged siblings and collapsed roots were decoded and validated, then read or copied again solely to stage their free records. Reuse that validated transaction state and remove the redundant free wrapper, preserving overflow reclamation checks and the V1 format.

A regression reproduces six page reads before the fix and five afterward. It also proves corrupt sibling refusal leaves bytes unchanged and successful root collapse reopens with the other records intact.

Validation: 39 regular storage tests, three adapter tests, the Rust 1.91 regression, native/Wasm Clippy, formatting, documentation links and dependency checks pass. The 320,000-operation differential campaign passes against upstream and the independent model. Full local release CI was not run.

Fresh before/after benchmark builds pass both suites with exact repeats and unchanged capacities/results. Mixed row/index instructions improve 0.0078%/0.0106%. Across 506 matrix cases, 42 improve, 460 are unchanged and four increase (at most 0.0128%); wins against upstream remain 381/506. Details and artifact identities are recorded in docs/design/canonical-workloads.md under Validated node reclamation.

Pending notes are 0.4.1; package versions and dependency selections are unchanged.

issue.body:
Mixed workloads previously constructed values for reads and deletes, then discarded those values inside the measured interval; scans retained an entirely unused batch. Prepare only the keys, values or bounds each operation consumes, and share the unchanged target-ID schedule between preparation and model updates.

Matrix scans now append borrowed keys directly into one output buffer for both engines, removing temporary per-key vectors while preserving lazy value loading. This PR is stacked on #7 and contains only benchmark changes and their notes; merge #7 first, then retarget this PR to main.

Validation: native all-target/Wasm benchmark Clippy, the host protocol test, formatting, documentation links and dependency checks pass. Both benchmark suites pass 2,280 measurements with exact repeats, matching model/results and unchanged stable capacities. Heap capacities change. The engine-only baseline rebuild is byte-identical across worktrees. Full local release CI was not run.

All 46 matrix key-scan cases improve for both engines; our reductions range from 12.9% to 86.0%. These fixture changes establish a new baseline rather than an algorithm speedup: our mixed row/index totals increase 0.9300%/0.0887%, and one mixed row scan increases 87.9389%. Upstream mixed rows increase 1.0231% and indexes decrease 0.0905%. The full comparison and artifact identities are recorded in docs/design/canonical-workloads.md under Benchmark input and key projection cleanup.

Pending notes remain 0.4.1. Package versions, dependency selections, wire IDs and CSV labels are unchanged.

+## Validated node reclamation
+
+The 0.4.1 patch stages free records for already decoded merge siblings and
+collapsed roots without reading them again. Overflow reclamation retains its
+validated page buffer and separate checks. A merging/root-collapse regression
+fails at six page reads on 0.4.0 and passes at five after the change. Corrupt
+sibling bytes still refuse deletion without writes; successful deletion audits
+and reopens with all other records intact. The V1 format is unchanged.
+
+All 39 regular storage tests, three public adapter tests, native/Wasm Clippy
+and the Rust 1.91 regression pass. The 320,000-operation extended differential
+campaign against upstream and the heap model passes. Full release CI is not run.
+
+Fresh baseline and engine-only builds use identical Cargo.lock selections,
+Rust 1.99, IC Memory 0.47, IC Testkit 0.51 and PocketIC server 16.0.0/client 16.1.0
+on Linux. Both builds pass 2,024 matrix and 256 mixed measurements, with exact
+repeats and unchanged heap/stable capacities and result sizes. Paired engines
+return matching result sizes; mixed operations also check their heap model.
+
+| Mixed workload | Our baseline | Our engine patch | Change |

+506 matrix cases, 42 improve, 460 are unchanged and four increase. The best is
+row_inline/remove (-4.3108%); the worst is index_full_root/remove (+0.0128%).
+Our count beating upstream remains 381/506. These are synthetic fixtures, not
+deployed IcyDB codec or recovery qualification.
